VITA is looking for a strategic partnership offering fully managed, secure, and compliant end-user services, while also providing flexibility to support management of both supplier-owned devices and Commonwealth-owned/leased devices. Additionally, VITA is also seeking supplier input on simplification of device offerings and other available transformative efforts that modernize the environment while containing costs. VITA will maintain a supplier-delivered End User Computing (EUC) model that builds on the current service framework at Commencement, through optimizing and modernizing services to align with current capabilities, demand, and operational realities. The Supplier will provide end-to-end service delivery, including device support, software support, troubleshooting, lifecycle management, and required financial and asset tracking processes (e.g., CMDB, GASB compliance) for all devices/workstations. Suppliers may propose value-added or premium services as optional capabilities available to agencies. During the life of the contract, Supplier will propose to VITA continual improvement of service/device offerings while meeting Customer needs and requirements, focusing on service quality, operational efficiency, and customer experience. The EUC supplier will be required to integrate as a full Tier 1supplier*. The EUC supplier may bring a suite of tools to manage the service platform, but all EUC provided tools shall not utilize proprietary tools or formats that hinder or prohibit integration into the MSI platform/VITA Toolkit. VITA and the MSI integrator shall have full, uninhibited real-time visibility into the content and configuration of all EUC provided tools.VITA anticipates a single award to one supplier for EUC services, while reserving the right to continually adjust the device ownership structure based on the best value and most suitable solution to the Commonwealth. VITA also reserves the right to issue a single award, multiple awards, or no award. All communications related to this forthcoming RFP should be directed to the Single Point of Contract (listed as the Buyer on this posting).More information on the Multi-Supplier model, including links to current Service Tower contracts, is available here: https://www.vita.virginia.gov/about/reports/multisupplier-model-information/ * VITAs Managed Environment is established by a multi-provider integrated model, led by a Multi-Sourcing Service Integrator (MSI) to deliver certain IT services to VITA and other Virginia Executive Branch Agencies. While VITAs Managed Environment is comprised of various and separate scopes of services provided by multiple Integrated Suppliers (also called Service Tower Suppliers), the multi-provider model requires coordination, cooperation and integration among the Integrated Suppliers. These suppliers must work together toward the common goal of providing uninterrupted, high-quality services to VITA & the Commonwealth. In this regard, the participants must perform their services, interact, and cooperate with each other in a manner that, as a foremost guiding principle, first considers the best interests of VITA & the Commonwealth.

The proposed restoration shall utilize a Priority 2 approach. Priority 2 restoration involves constructing a new bankfull channel within a newly excavated lower floodplain bench. All denuded areas shall be re-seeded, fertilized, matted, and planted with native woody stems and herbaceous cover. records.description: Lee County is in search for bidders to replace the waste pipe in the jail/courthouse. Scope of Work includes: Provide all necessary labor, material, equipment, supervision, etc. for waste pipe improvements within designated areas of the Lee County Jail/Courthouse building. Base bid includes removal and replacement of existing cast-iron waste and vent piping in inmate cell pods “A” and “B”, removal and replacement of existing cast-iron waste and vent piping in the common utility chase serving public fixtures in inmate cell pods “A” and “B”, and addition of a floor sink and lint interceptor in laundry room 1018. Alternate 1 includes removal and replacement of approximately sixteen (16) linear feet (to be verified by Contractor) of existing cast-iron waste piping below the ground floor slab in men's locker room 1035, replacement of two (2) existing tank toilets in men's locker room 1035 and one tank toilet in women's locker room 1058 with flush valve toilets, and providing new domestic water lines to the new toilets. Alternate 2 includes removal and replacement of approximately fifty (50) linear feet (to be verified by Contractor) of existing cast-iron waste piping below the ground floor slab between offices 1038 and 1061.
